pr_title: Remove ipaddress check in AndroidTV config flow
pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

In config flow there is a check to verify that the hostname is a valid ipv4 address and that the address is not already configured. Because the check for already configured device is done based on unique ID, this check is useless, and can create issue in case of host associated to ipv6 address. In case that hostname is invalid the error will occur during connection test. 
With this PR this check is removed.

issue_context.title: Cannot setup AndroidTV IPv6 only host
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I've set up a DNS AAAA record that points to the IPv6 address of my AndroidTV device. There's no A record (no IPv4).
When using tthis IPv6 host name in the device integration that was automatically discovered, I get an error :
`Invalid hostname or IP address`

This is because of the check in config_flow.py lines 155-157:
```
            ip_address = await self.hass.async_add_executor_job(_get_ip, host)
            if not ip_address:
                return self._show_setup_form(user_input, "invalid_host")
```
whiche fails with an IPv6 only host.
It's 2022: time to fully support IPv6!
Thanks

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.2.7

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

The behaviour is due to line 65 in config_flow.py:
`return socket.gethostbyname(host)`
The method gethostbyname return the IPv4 address only: [https://pythontic.com/modules/socket/gethostbyname](https://pythontic.com/modules/socket/gethostbyname)

Maybe the method getaddrinfo should be used instead?

This is an example to get the IPv6 address from hostname:
```
def get_ip_6(host, port=0):
     # search for all addresses, but take only the v6 ones
     alladdr = socket.getaddrinfo(host,port)
     ip6 = filter(
         lambda x: x[0] == socket.AF_INET6, # means its ip6
         alladdr
     )
     # if you want just the sockaddr
     # return map(lambda x:x[4],ip6)
     return list(ip6)[0][4][0]
```
Yes, it make sense. I do not consider this condition, thinking that IPv4 would be always available. I will think about this.

review_comments: Should this check be removed too, considering the check for unique_id below?
Uhm, that's was my dilemma. Probably identical host does not make sense and could just create confusion because also used in the name, so my idea was that is better to block this case.
